latin.455: Addis, idem demonstrari ex promissione Evangelii illic inserta vers. 15. de semine mulieris, Christo scilicet vindice generis humani, contrituro caput serpentis. Quemadmodum ex poena communi infertur peccatum fuisse commune, sic ex Remedio communi ad delendum illud peccatum, sequitur illud peccatum fuisse omnibus commune. At primum commune fateor peccatum, sed situm, non in imputatione peccati actualis Adami, sed in corruptione omnibus insita; & commune factum, non imputatione divina, sed generatione carnali.
latin.456: Alioqui Diabolus sua tentatione unicum hominem peccatorem effecisset, Deus (cogitans totus cohorresco) sua illa imputatione reliquos omnes; cujus imputationis demonstra si potes vel necessitatem, vel justitiam. Caeterum quantumvis commune sit remedium, tamen non applicatur, non imputatur ulli adulto, nisi consentienti ac per fidem illud apprehendenti, nec nostrum est nisi Christi & Dei dono. Donari autem a Deo nobis peccatum actuale Adami absit ut credam.
latin.457: Vis autem imputationem peccati actualis Adami antecedere omnem nostrum sive habitualem, sive actualem consensum. Tuam igitur potius sententiam commune hoc remedium evertit, quam firmat.
latin.458: Quid quod mihi arma ministrat tuae isti imputationi funesta? Sic enim ratiocinor. Id cui remedium commune opponitur, vel est ipsum commune malum vel causa cur sit malum commune. Opponitur hoc loco remedium commune serpenti; nec est serpens ipsum commune malum. Ergo serpens est causa cur sit malum commune.
latin.459: Non est autem causa mali communis, nisi aut illud ipse omnibus inspiraverit, aut saltem tale malum in uno produxerit, quod sponte, per se, naturali vi sua sese in omnes ut venenum, ut pestis, diffuderit, & propagaverit. Imputatio, inflictio poenae Dei opus est, non serpentis antiqui.
latin.460: Si igitur peccatum actuale non est omnibus commune, nisi imputatione; quia Deus illud omnibus imputat, nec est in nobis peccatum originale seu vitium inhaerens, nisi quia nobis in poenam actualis illius imputati a Deo infigitur, mali communitas non est a serpente; Nec ista privatio justitiae originalis & corruptio haereditaria virus est serpentis, quod nobis afflavit, sed (quod horret animus meus dicere) Dei effectum & opus.

pass_a.455: Next you claim the same from the Gospel promise at v. 15 about the woman's seed—Christ who will crush the serpent's head as the race's avenger. From a shared penalty you infer a shared sin; likewise from a shared Remedy to wipe that sin away you infer the sin was everyone's. Placeus grants a first shared sin, but located in the corruption set in all, not in charging Adam's actual deed; and made shared by fleshly generation, not by God's charging it.
pass_a.456: Otherwise the Devil by his temptation would have made only one human a sinner, God (Placeus shudders wholly at the thought) by that imputation all the rest—show if you can that imputation's necessity or justice. Besides, however common the remedy, it is not applied or imputed to any adult except one consenting and grasping it by faith, nor is it ours except by Christ's and God's gift. Far be it that Placeus believe God gifts us Adam's actual sin.
pass_a.457: Yet you require that charge of Adam's actual sin to come before any consent of ours—habit or act. That shared remedy therefore topples your thesis more than it props it up.
pass_a.458: Worse for you: the same move hands Placeus weapons deadly to that charge. His chain: whatever a shared remedy fights is either the shared ill itself or what makes the ill shared. Here the remedy fights the serpent; the serpent is not itself the shared ill. So the serpent is why the ill is shared.
pass_a.459: And he counts as cause of a shared ill only if he breathed it into everyone, or at least bred in one an ill that of itself, by its own natural force, ran through all like venom or plague. Charging and laying on penalty are God's doing, not the old serpent's.
pass_a.460: So if Adam's actual deed is shared only because God charges it to all, and original vice sticks in us only as the penalty of that charged deed, then the sharing of the ill does not come from the serpent; nor is loss of original rightness and inherited corruption the serpent's breath on us, but—Placeus almost cannot say it—God's own effect and work. Tip before the death-as-devil reply / Psalm 32.

455: You add that the same is demonstrated from the promise of the Gospel inserted there in verse 15 concerning the seed of the woman, Christ namely the avenger of the human race, who will crush the serpent's head. Just as from a common penalty it is inferred that the sin was common, so from a common Remedy for blotting out that sin it follows that that sin was common to all. But I confess a first common sin, yet seated not in the imputation of Adam's actual sin, but in corruption implanted in all; and made common not by divine imputation, but by carnal generation.
456: Otherwise the Devil by his temptation would have made a single human a sinner, God (thinking it I wholly shudder) by that imputation of his all the rest; of which imputation show if you can either the necessity or the justice. For the rest, however common the remedy may be, yet it is not applied, not imputed to any adult, except to one consenting and apprehending it by faith, nor is it ours except by the gift of Christ and of God. But that Adam's actual sin should be given to us by God—far be it that I believe.
457: But you want the imputation of Adam's actual sin to precede all our consent, whether habitual or actual. Therefore this common remedy rather overturns your opinion than confirms it.
458: What of this—that it even supplies me arms fatal to that imputation of yours? For I reason thus. That against which a common remedy is set is either the common evil itself or the cause why the evil is common. In this place the common remedy is set against the serpent; and the serpent is not itself the common evil. Therefore the serpent is the cause why the evil is common.
459: But he is not the cause of a common evil unless either he himself breathed that evil into all, or at least produced in one such an evil as of itself, by its own natural force, spread and propagated itself into all like poison, like a plague. Imputation, the infliction of penalty, is God's work, not the ancient serpent's.
460: If therefore actual sin is not common to all except by imputation—because God imputes it to all—and original sin or inhering vice is not in us except because it is fixed in us by God as the penalty of that imputed actual, the community of evil is not from the serpent. Nor is that privation of original justice and hereditary corruption the serpent's virus which he breathed upon us, but (which my mind shudders to say) God's effect and work.
